subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A test cross of a heterozygote with a homozygous recessive individual is expected to give a phenotypic ratio of:
questions.explain: Crossing Aa with aa yields half Aa and half aa, a 1:1 phenotypic ratio.

questions.q: A student tests a solution with Benedict's reagent and observes no colour change on heating, then performs the Benedict's test again after boiling with dilute acid and neutralising, obtaining a brick-red precipitate. This indicates:
options: a non-reducing sugar such as sucrose was present
a reducing sugar was present originally
questions.explain: Acid hydrolysis breaks a non-reducing sugar into reducing monosaccharides, which then give a positive Benedict's result.

questions.q: Disruptive selection differs from the other types because it:
options: Favours both extreme phenotypes at the expense of intermediates
questions.explain: Disruptive selection favours both extremes and selects against intermediate phenotypes, potentially leading to two distinct groups.

questions.q: How many hydrogen bonds form between guanine and cytosine in DNA?
questions.explain: Guanine and cytosine pair via three hydrogen bonds, whereas adenine and thymine pair via two.

questions.q: Using the data above (q = 0.1), the frequency of heterozygous carriers (2pq) is:
The genetic code is described as 'degenerate'. This means that:
options: Each codon codes for more than one amino acid
Most amino acids can be coded for by more than one codon
Some codons do not code for any amino acid
questions.explain: Degeneracy means most amino acids are specified by more than one triplet codon.

questions.q: Continuous variation (e.g. human height) is typically caused by:
options: Many genes acting together (polygenic) plus environmental influence
A single gene with two alleles
questions.explain: Continuous variation is polygenic, with many genes and the environment producing a range of phenotypes.

questions.q: Haemophilia is more common in males than females because:
options: Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is expressed
The allele is carried on the Y chromosome
questions.explain: The recessive allele is X-linked, and males (XY) express it with only one copy as they have no second X to mask it.

questions.q: In semi-conservative replication, each new DNA molecule consists of:
options: One original strand and one new strand
Fragments of both original strands recombined
questions.explain: Each daughter molecule conserves one parental strand which acts as a template for one newly synthesised strand.

questions.q: A tRNA anticodon is 5'-UAC-3'. The mRNA codon it pairs with is:
questions.explain: Antiparallel complementary base pairing of anticodon 5'-UAC-3' gives codon 5'-GUA-3'.
